meta.title: Tom's Paper Boat
meta.textType: story: a cartoon story with key words

paragraphs: On Saturday morning, Tom made a small boat from paper. He drew a yellow sail on it. "I want to sail it on the lake," he said. He invited Ben and Lily to come with him. Ben had a red boat, too. Pip ran in front of them on the road to the park. Lily carried a bag with bread and water.

It was a windy day at the lake. The sun was bright, and the water was blue. Ben put his boat on the water. It sailed quickly, and it looked big and strong. Tom put his boat on the water, too. It went round and round, and then it stopped. "Everything is wrong!" said Tom. "Which part of the boat is wrong?" asked Lily. Tom looked at the sail and the water. "I don't know," he said. Pip looked at the little boat and said, "Woof!" Tom was sad.

"Your sail is too small," said Ben. "Make a bigger sail for the wind." Lily had some big paper in her bag. She gave it to Tom. Tom made a new sail, and Ben helped him. They colored it yellow, and Pip watched them. Then Tom put the boat on the water again. It sailed slowly, and then it sailed on and on. "That's better!" said Ben. "Thank you, Lily," said Tom. The two boats sailed on the blue water. Tom, Ben, and Lily smiled, and Pip jumped up and down.
text.summary: Tom makes a paper boat and invites Ben and Lily to the lake. His boat does not sail well, so Lily gives him a bigger piece of paper.
